acceptedAnswer.text: Google Ads management is the work of running paid campaigns across Google Search, Shopping, YouTube and automated formats such as Performance Max, aimed at people already looking for what you sell.

mainEntity.name: How does Google Ads work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We separate brand search from everything else, build search and shopping around intent, fix the product feed, give automated campaigns clean inputs, and review the account every week. Results are judged on contribution margin, not on what a platform reports.

Your ad spend is paid to Google and sits outside our fee. We quote our fee after a call, once we have seen the account and agreed what we will run. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your spend and your margins.
No. We cannot guarantee clicks, rankings or sales, because demand and competition are outside anyone's control. We commit to a clear structure, accurate tracking and honest reporting.

D2C brands that sell products people search for, B2B companies whose buyers search for the problem, and colleges and schools whose families search for courses. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on contribution margin and repeat purchase, B2B on the cost of a qualified lead, education on enquiries, visits and admissions.

mainEntity.name: What do you need from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Access to your Google Ads and Analytics accounts, your product feed or catalogue, your margins or the value of a qualified lead, and the landing pages you want to use.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: Google shows your ads to people who are searching, so quality of structure and data decides the result. Each stage below is where spend leaks, and how we run it.

stages.breaks: Mixing brand and non-brand searches in one campaign.
stages.why: Brand searches convert easily and can make a campaign look better than it is, hiding wasted spend on generic terms.
stages.does: We keep brand search separate from generic and competitor searches, and structure campaigns by intent so each can be judged fairly.

stages.breaks: Uploading a product feed and leaving it alone.
stages.why: For Shopping, the feed is the ad. Weak titles, missing attributes and wrong prices limit what shows and who clicks.
stages.does: We clean and optimise the feed: titles, attributes, categories and pricing, so the right products show for the right searches.

stages.breaks: Handing budget to automation with no direction.
stages.why: Automated campaigns are only as good as the assets, audience signals and conversion data you give them.
stages.does: We feed them strong creative assets, clear audience signals and accurate conversion data, and check where the spend actually goes.

stages.breaks: Ignoring video, or running it with no follow-up.
stages.why: Video builds interest before the search, but only pays off if it is joined up with the rest of the account.
stages.does: We use video to reach and warm audiences, and connect it to search and shopping so interest turns into demand.

stages.why: Reported conversions can include low-value actions and repeats, and leave out cost of goods and returns.
stages.does: We set up conversion tracking that matches real business value, and judge campaigns on contribution margin or the cost of a qualified lead.

good.t: People already search for what you sell, and you want that demand captured at a profit.
good.why: Search and shopping work best when buyers have intent, so they suit D2C brands, B2B companies with a clear problem to solve, and colleges and schools that families search for.

not.t: You want Google to create demand from nothing, or a guaranteed ranking.
not.why: Search captures demand that exists; if nobody is looking yet, other channels or brand work should come first, and we will say so.
